name: Oil India Ltd
tagline: India's #2 upstream E&P PSU - cheap, dividend-paying, leveraged to North-East gas monetisation and higher crude - but a ~Rs 80,000 Cr large-cap whose size and flattish production keep it well outside the 10x/100x mandate.
business_overview: State-controlled upstream oil & gas producer focused on Assam/Arunachal (North-East India) producing fields, with a crude & product pipeline network, a stake in Numaligarh Refinery (NRL), city-gas and overseas assets. Seeded via the theme-scan 2026-09-09 (user-authorised 1x no-self-discovery bypass) under the oilfield-services / drilling & exploration-capex theme. Like ONGC, it is a capex setter for the services chain rather than a levered proxy.
fundamentals_table: Mid-teens ROCE typical for the cycle; ROE low-double-digits
Moderate consolidated debt (NRL expansion, acquisitions); serviceable
Low-single-digit to high-single-digit P/E through the cycle; ~5%+ dividend yield
fundamentals_narrative: A cheaper, smaller ONGC with a sharper North-East gas angle: the North East Gas Grid (Phase 1 inaugurated March 2026) and rising regional evacuation capacity should let Oil India monetise more Assam gas over the next few years, and NRL's refinery expansion adds downstream earnings. But it remains a ~Rs 80,000 Cr PSU with modest organic volume growth, windfall-tax exposure and government-driven capital allocation. Undemanding valuation and yield, not a compounding story.
technical_read: Not pulled - mid-range within a wide 52-week band; size math governs the verdict.
sentiment_summary: No dedicated Oil India ValuePickr thread resolved with confidence; the HOEC thread (topic 1581) references Oil India's DNPL/DFL pipeline decisions as a swing factor for North-East gas players. topic_slug left null; web/fundamentals-based assessment, appropriate for a covered large-cap PSU.
community_signal: No trusted-user activity. Sector tenor: 'cheap, gas-grid optionality, windfall-tax and PSU discount'.
bse_notes: No SEBI/fraud action. Windfall tax on domestic crude applies. DNPL pipeline recently designated a captive line for Oil India gas to Numaligarh; Duliajan Feeder Line to become a common carrier but ~18 months out - near-term evacuation is still a constraint on regional volumes.
bull_case: North East Gas Grid + captive DNPL line should lift Assam gas monetisation over FY27-29
NRL refinery expansion adds downstream earnings; overseas assets provide optionality
bear_case: ~Rs 80,000 Cr market cap - 10x/100x is arithmetically out of reach
Organic production growth modest; reserve replacement a perennial issue
Windfall tax caps crude-spike upside; PSU capital allocation (subsidy sharing, NRL funding)
Near-term North-East gas volumes still evacuation-constrained (DFL ~18 months away)
verdict_headline: Cheap North-East-gas-levered upstream PSU with real grid-driven monetisation optionality, but a large-cap with flattish volumes and no named structural inflection - size math makes 'neither' the honest call. Conviction Low-Medium.
verdict_reasoning: four_box: tailwind weak (North-East gas-grid monetisation and higher prices are real but incremental and partly evacuation-gated; not a structural growth engine), tam no (genuine large-cap ~Rs 80,000 Cr - cannot deliver the required multiple), moat yes (dominant North-East acreage, integrated pipeline + NRL stake), valuation yes (mid-single-digit P/E, ~5%+ yield - thesis not priced in) -> score 2.5

Score 2.0-2.5: valuation box = yes technically permits a label, but this is a genuine large-cap and the gas-grid ramp is an incremental volume story, not a specific named management/structural inflection of the kind the large-cap exception requires. Label kept 'neither'.
Conviction Low-Medium: valuation, yield and a credible (if gated) North-East gas catalyst put it above Low; size, flattish volumes and PSU constraints keep it below Medium
